synthesis: The ticket conflates two distinct failure modes under "Kit User Path shows no data". The verified, code-level root cause of the reported symptom is that KitUserPathController::paths() sources its route EXCLUSIVELY from clarity.sc_positions via KitRangePathsQuery — a different table from clarity.kit_scan_paths, which the reporter checked and correctly found populated for all 8 kits. Measured against production ClickHouse: 6 of the 8 org-469 kits have ZERO sc_positions rows in the last 30 days, kit 10588 has GPS for a single day (2026-08-13) only, and only kit 15349 has a healthy continuous track through today. So for nearly every kit the customer selects, KitRangePathsQuery legitimately returns zero segments and the frontend shows a blank map with a 'no data found' toast — exactly the reported symptom — while kit_scan_paths (read only by the Scout driver app, never by this admin page) is fully populated. Org 469 is therefore a live customer instance of the scan-only-kit class ALREADY tracked as DEV-2222, whose fix is implemented on an unmerged draft PR #320. The reporter's other two hypotheses (missing permission; all kits soft-deleted in kit_metadata) are plausible but NOT verifiable by this pipeline, and the permission hypothesis predicts a different symptom (page inaccessible) than the one reported.

PRIOR ART: PR #320 (branch claude/dev-2222-cf9a90) carries a review-hardened implementation of the fallback — 4 code files, +465 lines of tests, and FIVE adversarial review rounds. Its settled decisions must not be re-litigated: (a) trigger is zero RENDERED SEGMENTS, not zero raw rows; (b) $localStart/$localEnd captured BEFORE Carbon::utc() mutates in place, because KitScanPathsQuery wants LOCAL wall-clock; (c) tier-1 and tier-2 both use cachedHandle() (throws) not query() (swallows Throwable to []); (d) a tier-1 CH outage is 503, a genuine over-budget count is 422; (e) tier-2 rows accumulate into a local list and merge only after the loop, so a mid-loop throw cannot ship truncated rows as a 200; (f) a tier-2 failure degrades to tier-1-only and never wipes kits that ARE rendering; (g) tier-2 is deliberately OUTSIDE MAX_RENDER_POINTS (ratified); (h) name/color come from the resolved Kit, never the CH row; (i) the CH-decoded path is json_encode'd once, not spliced verbatim like tier-1's pre-encoded path_json.

REVIEW HISTORY: DEV-2222's gate NEVER passed — RN1 78, RN2 72, RN3 80, RN4 78, RN5 74 against a >=90 threshold. RN2 went DOWN because a self-authored guard was itself defective (it keyed off 'counted points but zero segments', but countPoints() counts PRE-SPLIT and <2-point segments are dropped, so that shape is legitimate and common). Do not reintroduce that guard; a pin test exists for exactly this.

R3+R7 INTERACTION (driver-spotted, needs a decision): per-day fallback makes the day key load-bearing. R7 records that trip_date is UTC-dated on the fallback tier but viewer-local-dated on the continuous tier. A per-day set-difference across two different day definitions will mis-diff at day boundaries — double-rendering or dropping a day. So R3 cannot be implemented correctly without making both tiers agree on the day key. Prefer normalizing the fallback tier's trip_date in the CONTROLLER (keeps the shared KitScanPathsQuery untouched, so the Bird's Eye and Scout Map co-callers see zero blast radius) rather than changing the shared query, which is why R7 was originally left alone.

OPEN RESIDUALS worth folding in while here (they scored in RN3-RN5): R4 near-tautological fallback name/color test; R6 scanPathRow() emits invalid JSON if json_encode returns false; plus RN5's 'TTL fork' and 'vacuous tier-2 test' mediums. Fixing these is cheap and they are known repeat scorers.

PROCESS: RN5's claude3 H1 was 'review-state/journal scores inside diff' — DEV-2222's ~1200 lines of docs/investigations artifacts were in the PR diff and reviewers graded them as part of the change. Keep DEV-2441's artifacts tight and expect the same effect.

Org 469 evidence STRENGTHENS R1's general severity even though it does not block this customer: 151 kits at the org, 6 of 8 sampled are scan-only — consistent with the 'Premier: ~37 GPS vs ~141 scan paths' production shape cited in DEV-2341. Record this on DEV-2341 when closing it.

SECURITY (driver-spotted, must not be missed): KitScanPathsQuery currently uses $timezone only via Carbon::parse(), which is safe. Interpolating it into raw SQL for toDate(timestamp, '<tz>') makes it an injection vector — $user->timezone resolves from $this->dti['timeZone'], which is user-influenced JSON. It MUST be validated against timezone_identifiers_list() first, exactly as KitRangePathsQuery::safeTimezone() already does. Note KitScanPathsQuery already addslashes() $layer, so the class has precedent for treating these arguments as untrusted.

R3 DESIGN (driver): implement the diff as per-(kit_id, local trip_date) coverage rather than per-kit-whole-window. Build a covered[kit_id][YYYY-MM-DD] map from tier-1 segments, enumerate the window's local days, skip any kit whose covered-day count already spans every window day (so a GPS-healthy org still issues no tier-2 read at all — preserving PR #320's 'fallback fires only for the minority' allocation property), then issue ONE batched tier-2 read for the remaining kits and drop any row whose (kit_id, trip_date) tier 1 already renders. This subsumes R1 for free: a mapping-less kit has no tier-1 coverage, so all of its days fall back.
